catalogNote: This page tracks high-frequency skill patterns rather than one-off marketplace entries. The goal is to capture the reusable skill shapes teams keep shipping across coding, research, orchestration, and delivery agents in April 2026.
architectureNote: There is no single universal skill package, but the shape repeats across ecosystems: a short manifest or instruction entrypoint, optional scripts or tools, supporting references, and a small amount of test or example material.

lifecycle.title: Intent match
lifecycle.description: The agent compares the user request against skill descriptions, triggers, or explicit slash invocations to decide whether a reusable skill should activate.

lifecycle.title: Context loading
lifecycle.description: Only the skill entrypoint and the small set of supporting files needed for the current task are loaded, which keeps long reference material cheap until it is relevant.

lifecycle.title: Workflow execution
lifecycle.description: The skill can call scripts, tools, prompts, or graph nodes to apply a repeatable playbook such as code review, triage, research, or release preparation.

lifecycle.title: Shaped output
lifecycle.description: A good skill constrains the final output with clear quality bars, formatting rules, and completion criteria so the result is predictable across repeated runs.

refreshWorkflow.title: How we keep the list fresh
refreshWorkflow.description: The source of truth stays versioned in Data\SeedData\skills.json. We refresh the page by re-reviewing official docs, reference repositories, and the skill patterns that continue to appear across public agent ecosystems.
refreshWorkflow.cadence: Monthly review, plus targeted updates after major agent releases
signals: A major ecosystem ships a new skills feature, manifest format, or packaging convention.
A workflow pattern starts appearing across several ecosystems instead of a single vendor stack.
Official docs or starter repositories deprecate an older skill shape or recommend a new one.
steps: Review official skills, agents, or orchestration docs before editing any curated entry.
Validate every documentation and repository link with Scripts\refresh-skills-links.ps1.
Update the JSON review label, architecture notes, and any affected skill patterns.
Rebuild the site and visually verify the Skills page before publishing.

categories.name: Claude Code skill patterns
categories.description: High-frequency repo-local skills built around SKILL.md playbooks and optional helper scripts.

skills.name: Code Review Gate
skills.description: A reusable review playbook that applies repo rules, surfaces blocking issues first, and standardizes review output.
skills.adoptionSignal: Frequently shared as a project skill because every team wants the same review bar without pasting a full checklist into each session.

skills.name: Repo Audit Playbook
skills.description: A structured skill for auditing architecture, dependencies, security notes, and operational drift inside an existing codebase.
skills.primaryUseCase: Fast codebase discovery and technical due diligence
skills.adoptionSignal: Common in platform teams and consulting workflows where the same repository audit needs to be rerun across many projects.

skills.name: Test Generation Workflow
skills.description: A skill that turns source files and conventions into targeted unit or integration test plans with a fixed quality checklist.
skills.primaryUseCase: Turning repeated testing prompts into one reusable instruction bundle
skills.adoptionSignal: Popular whenever teams need consistent test style, fixture usage, and coverage expectations across repositories.

categories.name: OpenAI Agents SDK patterns
categories.description: Code-backed agent skills that package tools, prompts, schemas, and guardrails for production workflows.

skills.name: Browser Research Agent
skills.description: A web-aware research skill that collects sources, extracts signals, and returns a structured brief with citations.
skills.adoptionSignal: One of the most repeated agent patterns because it combines tool use, guardrails, and structured output in a single reusable package.

skills.name: Retrieval QA Skill
skills.description: A retrieval-augmented skill that blends vector search, citations, and answer validation for internal knowledge bases.
skills.primaryUseCase: Knowledge-grounded answers over docs or product content
skills.adoptionSignal: Persists because most real agent deployments still need repeatable grounding and auditable answers.

skills.name: PR and Issue Triage Agent
skills.description: A triage skill that clusters repository events, assigns urgency, and drafts next actions for maintainers.
skills.primaryUseCase: Maintainer inbox reduction and backlog hygiene
skills.adoptionSignal: Widely reused where teams want tool-backed automation but still need explicit schemas and approval checkpoints.

categories.name: LangGraph skill patterns
categories.description: Stateful orchestration patterns for skills that branch, retry, or require approvals across several steps.

skills.name: Incident Commander Graph
skills.description: A graph-driven response skill that detects signals, routes tasks, and produces a live incident summary with state tracking.
skills.primaryUseCase: Operational incidents, escalations, and response loops
skills.adoptionSignal: High value whenever the skill must survive retries, branching, or partial progress rather than one linear prompt.

skills.name: Docs-to-Code Planner
skills.description: A planning skill that reads specs or documentation, builds intermediate state, and emits an implementation sequence.
skills.adoptionSignal: Useful when teams want planning, validation, and execution to stay connected instead of living in separate prompts.

skills.name: Stateful Support Router
skills.description: A routing skill that classifies requests, preserves conversation state, and hands work to the right downstream agent or human.
skills.primaryUseCase: Support, service desks, and triage-heavy help flows
skills.adoptionSignal: Common because routing skills usually need durable state and explicit branch logic once the happy path breaks.

categories.name: Microsoft Skills
categories.description: Real SKILL.md-based entries curated from the public microsoft/skills repository.

skills.name: applicationinsights-web-ts
skills.description: Instrument browser and web apps with the Application Insights JavaScript SDK for RUM, dependencies, exceptions, custom events, and browser-side GenAI traces correlated with backend observability.
skills.primaryUseCase: Frontend telemetry, RUM, and correlated tracing
skills.adoptionSignal: Useful when teams need production-grade browser instrumentation and want agent guidance tied directly to the Azure SDK skill catalog.

skills.name: continual-learning
skills.description: Guide and hook-based skill for implementing continual learning in coding agents through memory scoping, reflection patterns, and cross-session persistence.
skills.primaryUseCase: Agent memory, reflection, and learning across sessions
skills.adoptionSignal: Notable because it adds practical long-term learning to coding agents with a lightweight hook and a clear project-versus-global memory split.

skills.name: frontend-design-review
skills.description: Review and create production-grade frontend interfaces with strong design quality, accessibility, and design-system compliance checks.
skills.primaryUseCase: Frontend design reviews, accessibility audits, and UI quality gates
skills.adoptionSignal: High-value for teams that want memorable UI reviews backed by an explicit rubric instead of generic frontend feedback.
